cues.caption: Welcome back, champ!
cues.text: Hi champ, welcome back! Ready for something really cool today?

cues.caption: Last time: variable boxes · set · change
cues.text: Last time, you made variable boxes. Score, lives, and name. You learned to set them, and change them by one. Super useful!

cues.caption: Unit 3 · Building With Blocks
cues.text: We're still in Unit three, Building With Blocks. And this is chapter four.

cues.caption: Chapter 4 · Making Choices in Code
cues.text: It's called, Making Choices in Code.

cues.caption: Can code make choices too?
cues.text: You make choices all day long. Should I wear a sweater? Should I play, or do homework first? Hmm. But can a computer make choices too?

cues.caption: Yes! And you'll teach it how
cues.text: It can! And by the end of today, you'll teach it how.

cues.caption: School morning. Dark clouds!
cues.text: Picture this. It's a school morning, and you look out of the window. Dark clouds, everywhere.

cues.caption: "If raining, umbrella. Else, a cap."
cues.text: Your mum says, if it is raining, take an umbrella. Else, wear a cap.

cues.caption: Remember Unit 2? If-then stories!
cues.text: Does that sound familiar? Yes! In Unit two, we made if, then stories, just like this one.

cues.caption: Not raining. What do you do?
cues.text: So here's a question. What should you do if it's sunny, and not raining at all? Think.

cues.caption: Else = otherwise → wear a cap
cues.text: Wear a cap! That's the else part. Else means, otherwise. It's what you do when the answer is no.

cues.caption: Same thinking, now with blocks!
cues.text: And today, we'll build this exact same thinking, with coding blocks.

cues.caption: The question is called a CONDITION
cues.text: Every choice starts with a question. In code, we call it a condition.

cues.caption: A question with a yes or no answer
cues.text: A condition is a question with only two answers. Yes, or no. Like, is it raining? Or, is Billu touching the wall?

cues.caption: Yes = TRUE · No = FALSE
cues.text: Computers say it a little differently. Yes is called true. And no is called false.

cues.caption: If block: inside runs only when TRUE
cues.text: And the if block is the block that asks the question. It's shaped like a mouth, or a letter C, so other blocks can sit inside it. It runs those inside blocks, only when the condition is true.

cues.caption: if touching coin then change score by 1
cues.text: Let's read one together. If touching coin, then change score by one.

cues.caption: Pointy slot = condition · inside = action
cues.text: The blue part, touching coin, is the condition. It fits in this pointy slot. And the block tucked inside is what happens when it's true.

cues.caption: Touching coin? TRUE → score goes up
cues.text: Billu runs, and touches the coin. Is it touching coin? True! So the inside block runs, and the score goes up by one.

cues.caption: Missed it? FALSE → nothing happens
cues.text: Now Billu jumps right over the coin, and misses it. Touching coin? False. So the inside block is skipped. Nothing happens. The score stays the same.

cues.caption: if touching wall then bounce, else move 10
cues.text: Now let's add an else. If touching wall, then bounce. Else, move ten steps.

cues.caption: Not touching → FALSE → move 10 steps
cues.text: Billu is in the middle of the stage, far from the wall. Touching wall? False. So the else part runs. Move ten steps. Walk, walk, walk.

cues.caption: Touching wall → TRUE → bounce!
cues.text: Now Billu reaches the wall. Touching wall? True! So Billu bounces, and turns around.

cues.caption: One question, two paths
cues.text: See? It's just like the rain story from this morning. If raining, umbrella. Else, cap. One question, and two paths to choose from.

cues.caption: Game time: True or false?
cues.text: Let's play, true or false! Remember, true means yes, and false means no. I'll show you Billu, and you tell me the answer.

cues.caption: Touching wall? True or false?
cues.text: The condition is, touching wall. Here's Billu, right up against the wall. True, or false?

cues.caption: TRUE! Billu is touching the wall
cues.text: True! Billu is touching the wall, so it would bounce.

cues.caption: Touching wall? True or false?
cues.text: Same condition, touching wall. Now Billu is far away, in the middle. True, or false?

cues.caption: FALSE! So the else part runs
cues.text: False! Billu is not touching anything. So if there's an else, the else part runs, and Billu keeps walking.

cues.caption: Story: ball touches goal → crowd cheers
cues.text: Now let's match a story to a block. Story: when the ball touches the goal, the crowd cheers.

cues.caption: if touching goal then play cheer sound
cues.text: What's the question here? Touching goal! And what happens? Play a cheer sound. So the block is, if touching goal, then play cheer sound. Easy, right?

cues.caption: Dog barks only when it touches the cat?
cues.text: Your turn. A dog in a game should bark, only when it touches the cat. Which block is right? Touching edge, touching cat, or forever say woof?

cues.caption: if touching cat then say "Woof!"
cues.text: If touching cat, then say woof! The condition must be about the cat. Forever would bark all the time. So noisy!

cues.caption: Tip: one condition at a time
cues.text: One last tip. When you're starting out, check just one condition in each if block.

cues.caption: Too many questions at once = confusing!
cues.text: If you ask, is it raining, and is it Monday, and is it hot, all at once, it gets confusing, fast!

cues.caption: One question → one clear answer
cues.text: One question. One clear answer. True, or false. Simple code is easier to read, and easier to fix. Bigger programs can ask more later. But for now, one at a time.

cues.caption: Your turn: practice check
cues.text: Okay champ, practice check time. Just like the quiz.

cues.caption: Billu misses the coin. What happens?
cues.text: If touching coin, then add one to score. What happens when the character misses the coin? Pause, and think it through.

cues.caption: FALSE, no else → score stays the same
cues.text: Nothing changes! The condition is false, and there's no else part. So the inside block is skipped, and the score stays exactly the same. Great thinking!

cues.caption: Score 4 · jumps over the star · score = ?
cues.text: Bonus. If touching star, then change score by one. The score is four. Billu jumps over the star, without touching it. What's the score?

cues.caption: Still 4! Never touched → FALSE
cues.text: Still four! It never touched the star, so the condition was false. Brilliant!

cues.caption: TRUE → the inside blocks run
cues.text: Let's remember. If the condition is true, the blocks inside run.

cues.caption: FALSE → the else part runs
cues.text: Else runs when the condition is false. It means, otherwise.

cues.caption: One condition at a time
cues.text: Check one condition at a time. Keep it simple.

cues.caption: No else + FALSE = nothing happens
cues.text: And no else, plus a false condition? Nothing happens.

cues.caption: Chapter 4 done!
cues.text: Chapter four of Unit three, done! Your code can make choices now, champ. Super work!

cues.caption: Next: Quiz · Tap Finish
cues.text: Now let's see what you remember. Tap Finish, and try the quiz. You've got this!
